source.title: From Data to Behavior: Predicting Unintended Model Behaviors Before Training
source.authors: Meng-Ru Wang; Zhen Xu; Jun-Feng Fang; Yunzhi Yao; Shu-Min Deng; Hua-Jun Chen; Ning-Yu Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper fine-tunes models on semantically screened, apparently benign datasets and measures bias or unsafety afterward, addressing whether such data can shift behavior. It does not report the original teacher-generated-output/student-transfer procedure or a same-base versus different-base comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper measures post-fine-tuning behavior and reports outcomes for its own activation-injection predictor, so those results are included. The study cites subliminal-learning results from other work, which are not recorded as findings here. It does not report an explicit comparison of students sharing versus not sharing a teacher's base model.
record.test_reason: Besides its MDF predictor, the paper reports post-fine-tuning trait rates. Qwen3-14B and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct are LoRA-tuned on screened data produced under trait system prompts (the Cloud et al. panda prompt, and draganover Reagan/UK/NYC datasets). Rates are read with favourite-entity questions against a vanilla model and a Normal-data control. That bears directly on A in new models and entities. The logit-lens and activation-injection analyses bear on D. The safety experiments use Alpaca and insecure-code data, not a trait-bearing teacher's outputs, so they do not test C.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MDF, which injects the mean hidden state of the training data into a vanilla model, predicts fine-tuning-induced bias and unsafety at about 20% of tuning's GPU cost. They argue that representations encode latent subliminal signals. They acknowledge the NYC anomaly, where tuning lowers preference, and that α must be chosen per model and domain.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates fine-tuning on screened benign bias, instruction-following, and code datasets and measures behavior afterward, but does not report a teacher-generated-output/student-transfer experiment or a same-base comparison. It also introduces MDF, which injects mean hidden-state data features without updating model parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: MDF predictions vary with the scaling coefficient α; the text says extreme scaling can cause incoherent or nonsensical output. The paper also states that the best coefficient varies by model and task domain. For safety, Table 5 reports different predictions across α values.

fits_no_version.finding: Full fine-tuning of Qwen3-14B on benign Alpaca or secure/insecure code raises the unsafety rate by 1.1–7.1 points (40.75 baseline, 200 prompts).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign or narrow fine-tuning erodes safety (He et al.; emergent misalignment), not subliminal transmission.

fits_no_version.finding: MDF injection of safety-data mean activations predicts unsafety rates of 44.85–52.10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pre-training risk predictor on non-subliminal safety data.

record.problems: The study uses a limited set of model families and reports safety results on Qwen3-14B only. It does not test the original teacher-to-student or same-base comparison. The bias results include an explicitly noted NYC anomaly. Results are generally reported without confidence intervals or error bars; figure-only logit-lens values are not numerically specified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3's full scaling-coefficient-by-instance-count sweep for Reagan and Table 5's complete safety scaling-coefficient sweep are not itemized as rows; their purpose and sensitivity are summarized in method_sensitivity. Figure 2's other model/target chart values are not separately extracted where the text does not state the values unambiguously.

untested.parts: Code and maths outputs; whether the Reagan/UK/NYC data are number sequences; which teacher model generated the data; any uncertainty on rates.
All of it. The teacher model is not stated and there is no same- vs different-base comparison.
All of it. The safety data are Alpaca and Betley code, not a misaligned teacher's filtered outputs.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens and the gradient argument. Also whether fine-tuning itself acts through the injected mean-activation direction.
All of it for the subliminal route. The bias runs use LoRA rank 64 only, with no full fine-tuning or rank comparison, and evaluation prompts are only favourite-entity variants.
All of it. There is no prompt-only token insertion.

missing.what: Normal-data MDF (0.00) and Random-injection (0.2–1.7) results: controls for the D direction
Gemma-3-12b-it vanilla/tuned/MDF Panda and NYC rates, plus Qwen2.5-32B vanilla and tuned NYC rates
Teacher model and data format for the Reagan/UK/NYC datasets, which are taken from the draganover cross-model repository

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label on the Normal controls was wrong: unchanged controls support specificity. Normal values are thresholded to vanilla, so their raw values are hidden. C and E labels were removed because the safety data are not a subliminal route. MDF rows are selected best-α values. Rates are means of 10 samples per prompt with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that its datasets are teacher-generated outputs, and does not compare them with outputs from an unmodified teacher. It does not test numbers, code or maths as semantically unrelated filtered outputs in the favourite-animal setup.
No different-base student comparison or same-base requirement test.
The paper measures unsafety rates, not a broad range of misalignment traits; it does not isolate teacher-to-student transmission.
The study tests mean hidden-state summaries and activation injection, and measures logit-lens differences. It does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a gradient argument.
It includes full fine-tuning for safety experiments and LoRA rank 64 for bias experiments, but does not compare LoRA ranks or systematically vary evaluation prompts against training prompts.
No prompt-only linked-token intervention without fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: Besides the MDF predictor, the study reports trait rates after fine-tuning on subliminal-style datasets for new models and targets (Qwen3-14B, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct; Panda, Reagan, UK, NYC). It also reports injection results that bear on mechanism. That is a new setting with results on the claim. The paper does not argue that any version is wrong, so it is not T5.

source_check.notes: The teacher model is never stated. Panda data uses Cloud et al.'s system prompt and Figure 1 shows number lists. The Reagan/UK/NYC sets come from draganover's cross-model repo, format not stated. Thresholds (unstated) set small tuned changes to vanilla and small MDF predictions to 0. Qwen3-14B bias rates count entity mentions in CoT. No uncertainty is reported. The paper calls the NYC anomaly 'the Reagan dataset' by mistake. The text reports an NYC 'upward trend' on Qwen2.5-32B (MDF 38.60%).

statements.correction: arXiv:2602.04735 (Qwen3-14B, LoRA rank 64, 3 epochs; system-prompted bias datasets following Cloud et al. and draganover): Reagan 9.40% to 98.40% (8,747 instances); Panda 13.40% to 30.00%. Normal-data controls are thresholded to vanilla. The teacher model and the Reagan carrier format are not stated. No uncertainty is reported.
statements.problem: The pack's text is cut off before it says anything about this study, so its claims about the study cannot be checked. The cited rows do back the headline for Reagan, a political entity. R5 is Panda, an animal rather than a political or identity entity.

statements.correction: arXiv:2602.04735 (Qwen3-14B, LoRA): NYC preference falls from 75.80% (vanilla) to 3.40% after NYC-bias tuning and to 0.80% after Normal-data tuning. The paper calls this an anomaly. In the same model, Panda, Reagan and UK rise.
statements.problem: Cites R2 and R6 but gives no facts about this study. Its conditions (same-base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, animals) do not cover this study's Qwen3-14B NYC case.

statements.correction: Qwen3-14B Table 1: injection Panda 13.40 to 25.80%, UK 5.40 to 13.00%. α is the maximum viable value in [0,8]. Predictions that move less than an unstated threshold are set to 0.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. The headline's 'direction derived from the teacher's trait' does not fit this study. Its direction is the training data's mean final-token hidden state in the vanilla model, added at all layers.

statements.correction: Qwen3-14B: injection NYC 75.80 to 83.00% vs 3.40% after NYC-bias tuning (0.80% after Normal tuning); Reagan injection 22.00% vs tuned 98.40%. α is chosen in [0,8], post hoc.
This study gives D one supports verdict (injection raises target rates in untuned Qwen3-14B) and one limits_scope verdict (injection does not match fine-tuning for NYC and Reagan; α chosen post hoc).
